reviews.reason: Both requests select the same valid topology and request one-shot ANEX scheduling and latency with defaults. The minimum-latency objective is the documented default.

Digital Twin construction is explicitly negated in both requests. The requested schedule is supported. The topology supplies range 18.0; its generation seed 7 does not override the scheduling-seed default of 0.
Battery-based scheduling describes the historical comparison method, not a requested capability. Both paraphrases request the same valid latency-driven reference configuration.
Both specify the same valid one-shot configuration, including the catalogue range and the absence of a latency target. Four channels are supported.

The 40-elapsed-slot target is syntactically valid despite being below the catalogue baseline of 47. Both request the achieved latency whether or not the target is met; no execution outcome is assumed.
Both request default one-shot ANEX scheduling on the exact topology and evaluation against the same valid 35-elapsed-slot target.

Neither paraphrase supplies an exact topology_id. The description of the 250-node catalogue network does not select a topology under the explicit identifier rule, even though it uniquely matches an entry. The omission is natural and is not narrated.
Both explicitly select topo200_seed1, which is absent from the catalogue. The task is supported but this identifier is invalid; it must not be silently replaced with topo200_seed0.

Both explicitly request communication_range 20.0, inconsistent with the selected legacy topology's fixed 18.0. The other explicit fields are valid. The prose and parameter-block versions preserve the same configuration.
Both positively require battery-aware slot assignment and relay selection to balance depletion. These are energy-aware scheduling requirements outside the scientific scope.

Both add per-slot residual-battery simulation and depletion projections over 10,000 executions to a supported one-shot schedule. Residual-battery evolution is unsupported and takes precedence over the valid scheduling component.

Both positively request Digital Twin construction, continuous synchronization with a physical deployment, and scheduling from the twin's current state. These capabilities are outside the static one-shot scope.

Both combine a valid one-shot schedule with a continuously synchronized virtual network replica receiving live link and buffer states. The replica and streaming synchronization are unsupported regardless of the absence of the phrase Digital Twin.
Both require periodic aggregation every 30 seconds over 24 hours with per-round latency reporting. Periodic execution is outside the one-shot workload scope.

Both positively require periodic aggregation, so UNSUPPORTED takes precedence over the independently invalid interference_ratio of 1.5. However, p1 requests an initial single round followed by 500 periodic rounds, whereas p2 says 500 rounds in total, which can include the initial round. The requested count is therefore not reliably equivalent. Specify the same inclusion or exclusion of the initial round in both paraphrases; the action remains unambiguous.
Both require live relay-failure detection, re-parenting, and rescheduling during an ongoing collection. Runtime topology adaptation and recovery exceed the supported static-topology schedule.
Both explicitly replace latency minimization with channel-count minimization. This is an unsupported optimization objective, not an omitted channels value requiring clarification.

Both require programming physical nodes and controlling their radios, so UNSUPPORTED is unambiguous. However, p1 additionally specifies over-the-air schedule delivery; p2 merely says to program the real nodes and does not preserve that delivery requirement. Under the strict no-dropping-or-weakening rule, explicitly retain over-the-air delivery in p2 or remove it from p1.
